Traffic Commission Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the Traffic Commission, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The Traffic Commission will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the Traffic Commission (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The Traffic Commission will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead Traffic Commission regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

REVIEW OF TRAFFIC CONDITIONS AT RIO HONDO AVENUE BETWEEN VALLEY BOULEVARD AND STEELE STREET
SUMMARY
The Traffic Commission received a request from a resident to review traffic conditions and access to the alley on the east side of Rio Hondo Avenue between Valley Boulevard and Steele Street. A new 5,645 square foot shopping center development is being considered at the southeast corner of Rio Hondo Avenue and Valley Boulevard. Access to the project will be directly from Rio Hondo Avenue and from the alley. There are concerns regarding the backup of vehicles traveling northbound along Rio Hondo Avenue waiting at the Valley Boulevard intersection blocking the access to the alley and essentially the new center.
STAFF RECOMMENDATION
In response to the residentâ€™s request, a traffic investigation of the intersection at Rio Hondo Avenue and Valley Boulevard and of the segment of Rio Hondo Avenue between Valley Boulevard and Steele Street was done. A field visit was conducted to evaluate site-specific conditions, such as traffic volumes, back of queue, and collision history. In order to determine how much traffic the proposed shopping center would generate during peak hours a trip generation based on the 9th Edition Trip Generation Manual using standard traffic engineering rates for a shopping center was done.
It was observed that during peak travel times, vehicle delay/congestion on Rio Hondo Avenue approaching Valley Boulevard was heavy with northbound vehicles blocking the alley-way. Therefore, staff is recommending the installation of â€œKEEP CLEARâ€ pavement markings with limit lines in the northbound travel lane of Rio Hondo Avenue south of Valley Boulevard in front of the alley on the east side of Rio Hondo Avenue as well as a â€œDO NOT BLOCK INTERSECTIONâ€ sign opposite the â€œKEEP CLEARâ€ pavement legend for NB direction. This will allow access to the new development for employees, shoppers and emergency vehicles as well as access to others that use the alley for access.
Staff Report
B.
REVIEW OF TRAFFIC CONDITIONS AT DRIVEWAY EXIT OF FRANCES WILLARD ELEMENTARY SCHOOL PARKING LOT
SUMMARY
The Traffic Commission received a request from the principal of Frances Willard Elementary School for the installation of a â€œRIGHT TURN ONLYâ€ sign at the exit of the northern driveway of the parent/visitor parking lot which is utilized as a drop-off/pick-up zone and it is located south of the staff parking lot. The principal stated that vehicles currently exiting the driveway from the drop-off/pick-up zone are crossing over oncoming traffic to make a left turn onto Willard Avenue which poses a risk to the students and parents safety and also creates additional traffic since vehicles have to wait until it clears up to be able to make a left turn.
STAFF RECOMMENDATION
In response to the principalâ€™s request, a traffic investigation of the northern driveway of the parent/visitor parking lot was done. A field visit was conducted to evaluate site-specific conditions, such as turning movement counts, and a speed survey.
It was observed that during peak travel times, there is a-lot of vehicles traveling on Willard Avenue during peak school hours making it difficult for parents to exit the pick-up/drop-off parking lot and wait for a gap in traffic to turn left. Therefore, staff is recommending the installation of a â€œRIGHT TURN ONLYâ€ sign at the exit of the northern driveway of the parent/visitor parking lot which is utilized as a drop-off/pick-up zone and is located south of the staff parking lot. This will help improve the safety of motorists and pedestrians by directing parents to make a right turn instead of waiting for a gap in traffic to turn left out of the lot. Additional on-site improvement includes the addition of pavement arrows designating an entrance driveway and exit driveway as well as â€œENTER ONLYâ€ and â€œEXIT ONLYâ€ signage at the driveway gates.
Staff Report
